subject: Choosing bedroom colours and finishes
hook: The sample looked perfect. The wardrobe looked darker. Here's why.
ig:
The sample looked perfect. The wardrobe looked darker. It happens a lot, and it's easy to avoid.

Five rules for choosing fitted wardrobe colours:

1. Large areas read darker than a small sample.
2. Your bedroom's light changes everything. North-facing rooms cool colours down; south-facing ones warm them up.
3. Match to the floor, not the walls. Paint changes; carpet and flooring usually don't.
4. Sheen changes colour. Gloss looks brighter, super matt looks deeper.
5. Choose handles with the finish. Antique gold and matt black change the whole feel.

Our finishes include matt white, charcoal, matt black, black woodgrain and oak-effect, in matt, super matt and gloss, so it pays to see them side by side in your own room.

Save this for when you're choosing, and book a free, no-obligation consultation via the link in bio to see samples at home.
fb:
Choosing a colour for fitted wardrobes is one of the decisions people worry about most, and for good reason: it's a big surface you'll see every day.

A few things we always share: big areas look darker than samples, your room's light (north or south facing) changes how colours look, it's better to match to your flooring than your walls, gloss and super matt make the same colour look different, and handles should be chosen at the same time as the finish.
